title: Session Overview Pane
bottom_line: Type /sessions to open a side pane that lists every open Claude Code session on this machine, grouped by project, with its goal and state.

sections.heading: Type /sessions, or add auto on or off

blocks.title: What to type
blocks.caption: The first line opens the pane now. The other two switch automatic opening on or off.

blocks.title: What each form does and what it replies
rows: `/sessions`
Opens the pane, titled Sessions, with the keyboard on it. It refreshes every 3 seconds while open.
Sessions pane opened.
`/sessions` when the pane cannot be placed
The pane is open but not shown in place.
Sessions pane open but not placed: followed by the reason
`/sessions auto on`
Opens the pane, without taking the keyboard, on every new session, including after `/clear`. The choice is remembered.
Sessions pane will open on every new session.
`/sessions auto off`
Stops the automatic opening. The choice is remembered.
Sessions pane will no longer open automatically.

blocks.text: The pane shows every open Claude Code session on the machine in a side pane, grouped by project, with each session's goal and state.

sections.heading: Check that your setup can run the pane

cards.title: Claude Code that loads mods
cards.text: The plugin registers a TypeScript module through `hooks/hooks.json`, not a skill, so your Claude Code version must load plugin mods.

cards.title: tmux, if you want jumping
cards.text: Optional. Clicking a session switches your tmux client to it. Outside tmux the list is read-only.

cards.title: Session files under ~/.claude/
cards.text: It works wherever Claude Code keeps its session files under `~/.claude/`.

blocks.title: Nothing to configure
items: No environment variables and no plugin settings.

sections.heading: The pane groups sessions by project and marks each state

blocks.title: Example: three sessions in one project
blocks.code:
1 need you   1 running   1 idle

my-app  ~/workspace
  ◆ Fix login redirect
    waiting: permission prompt
  ● GDPR and PECR compliance audit
    worktree wt-1
  ○ Add pricing page

1: bg  2: cli  3: sdk-cli (hidden)

blocks.text: The top line counts sessions by state. Under it, each project heading shows the folder name in bold and its parent path dimmed. The last line of the example shows the type buttons, each with its number.

blocks.title: The four states
rows: waiting
The session waits for something, for example a permission prompt. These are the sessions that need you.
waiting: followed by what it waits for, or waiting: your reply when nothing more specific is known
running
The session is running.
none
idle
Finished, awaiting the next prompt.
none
ended
A leftover registry entry whose process is gone.
a dim ended line

blocks.title: How the list is arranged
items: The count line at the top shows how many sessions need you (waiting), and how many are running, idle and ended. A state with no sessions is left out.
Sessions are grouped by run directory. Home is shown as `~`.
Worktrees (`<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`) appear under their repo, with a line saying worktree and the worktree name.
Within a project, starred sessions come first, then waiting, running, idle and ended.
Projects are ordered with the most recently updated project first.
A dim today after the title marks a session active today.
This session's title is bold and tagged (this one).
With nothing to show, the pane says No sessions open.

sections.heading: Each session's goal comes from the best title available

blocks.title: Where the goal text comes from, first match wins
blocks.caption: A title you set with /rename always wins. A session with no goal at all shows Untitled session.

blocks.text: To set your own title, type `/rename <title>`.

sections.heading: Haiku names an untitled session from its first prompt

blocks.title: What is sent to a model
blocks.caption: On the first prompt of a session that has no title yet, up to the first 4000 characters go to Haiku.

blocks.title: Prompts it skips
items: Prompts that did not come from you.
Sessions that already have a title, for example one set with `/rename`.

sections.heading: Star, hide or jump to sessions from the pane

cards.title: Star a session
cards.text: Click the ☆ before a title to star it (★). Starred sessions lead their project. Stars are saved across restarts and shown in every open session within a few seconds.

cards.title: Hide a session type
cards.text: One toggle button per session type (`cli`, `bg`, `sdk-cli`, and so on) hides or shows that type. A hidden type is marked (hidden).

points.text: The choice is remembered across restarts.
It shows in every open session within a few seconds.

cards.title: Jump to a tmux session
cards.text: Click a session running in tmux to switch this tmux client to it (`tmux switch-client`). Sessions outside tmux, and ended ones, are not clickable.

blocks.title: Keyboard
items: The toggles have hotkeys `1` to `9`, in type order, shown on each button. At most 9 type buttons are shown.
The hotkeys work while the pane has the keyboard. `/sessions` opens it focused; otherwise click the pane or press ctrl+x tab.
Arrows scroll a tree taller than the pane.

blocks.title: The hint at the bottom of the pane
rows: The pane has the keyboard
Click ☆ to star a session, a title to jump to it (tmux only). "today" marks sessions active today. Number keys hide a type. Esc returns.
The pane does not have the keyboard
Press ctrl+x tab to use the number keys.

sections.heading: Open the pane on every new session with auto on

before.label: Default
before.text: The pane opens only when you run `/sessions`.

after.label: After /sessions auto on
after.text: The pane opens, unfocused, on every new session, including after `/clear`. It does not take the keyboard from the prompt. Run `/sessions auto off` to turn it off.

blocks.caption: The choice is remembered. Automatic opening happens only for interactive sessions.

sections.heading: Every default can be changed from inside Claude Code

blocks.title: Opinionated defaults
rows: The pane opens only when you run `/sessions`
`/sessions auto on` opens it, unfocused, on every new session (including after `/clear`); `/sessions auto off` turns that off
Untitled sessions are named by Haiku from their first prompt
`/rename <title>` sets your own title, which always wins
All session types are shown
the per-type toggle buttons or the `1`-`9` hotkeys

sections.heading: If the pane does not behave as expected

cards.title: Open but not placed
cards.text: The reply says Sessions pane open but not placed, followed by the reason.

cards.title: Couldn't switch to that pane
cards.text: A toast says Couldn't switch to that tmux pane when the tmux switch fails.

cards.title: A title is not clickable
cards.text: Only sessions running in tmux can be clicked. Sessions outside tmux, and ended ones, are not clickable.

cards.title: Number keys do nothing
cards.text: The hotkeys work while the pane has the keyboard.

points.text: Click the pane or press ctrl+x tab.

next_action.text: Type `/sessions` in a Claude Code session to open the pane.
next_action.detail: It opens with the keyboard on it and refreshes every 3 seconds. Press Esc to return to the prompt.
